title: National Portrait Gallery founded
documented_change: Founded to collect portraits of 'the most eminent persons in British history'; early trustees prioritised sitter significance over artistic merit.
why_it_matters: Establishes an unusually explicit selection principle centred on historical eminence.
what_remained: Portraiture serves historical understanding from the outset.

title: Moves to St Martin's Place
documented_change: The Gallery acquires its purpose-built home beside the National Gallery.
why_it_matters: Gives the institution a permanent national public presence.

title: Museums and Galleries Act
documented_change: The Act establishes the modern Board and statutory functions.
why_it_matters: Codifies duties to maintain, preserve, add to and exhibit the collection and promote understanding of British history through portraiture.
what_remained: The original concern with people in British history survives in broader statutory form.

title: Reopens after redevelopment
documented_change: The Gallery reopens following major capital redevelopment.
why_it_matters: Changes the visitor environment and institutional presentation, creating a point for pre/post comparison.
what_remained: The statutory collection and governance framework remain.

title: DCMS framework 2026–29
documented_change: A new framework spells out classification, appointments, financial controls and the DCMS relationship.
why_it_matters: Board elects Chair; trustees are PM-appointed, with two ex-officio trustees and an Artist Trustee; Director requires PM approval.
what_remained: The document creates no legal powers; the 1992 Act remains upstream.
